tweet: "As a woman in the military, you cant just quit the military. You let them win if you give up. We have to keep pushing, and changing, and fighting back to change these issue. You need to push back to be a woman in the military."

"As a woman in the military, I have been held back compared to my male peers. I have been insulted, assaulted, harassed, and passed on for positions. I dont think I can progress anymore You need to be able to progress to be a woman in the military."

"As a woman in the military, you are one of the few women around. Men comment saying, they "have something cute to look at" during the day. But also complain that we are distracting them when we wear our skirted uniform. You need to be a hypocrite to be a woman in the military."

"As a woman in the military, my harasser got away with no repercussions.  They told me I had to meet up with him for mediation so we could move on. Having PTSD didnt allow for me for be in the same room as him. You need to not be affected by others to be a woman in the military."

"As a woman in the military, I spent a lot of time crying in my room. You cant let anyone else see you, so you have to hold it in until your breaks. If they see you, you are weak. You need to hide when you cry to be a woman in the military."

"As a woman in the military, I spent 9 months in therapy. I was diagnosed with Post Traumatic Stress Disorder after spending 3 months being harassed. I was told to "just get over it" but struggle thinking about it. You need to "just get over it" to be a woman in the military."

"As a woman in the military, I had to stop eating in the galley. It was the one place on base where everyone was in the same room. Three times a day my anxiety went through the roof thinking about what my harasser would say. You need to eat off base to be a woman in the military."

"As a woman in the military, men are allowed to harass me at work. When I reported it to my chain of command, They ask me what I did to provoke him. You need to keep it to yourself to be a woman in the military."

"As a woman in the military, people often think I am a nurse or a clerk. People have handed me their pay sheet or asked me to file paperwork. They assume your job based off old gender roles in the military. You need to tell them "its not my job" to be a woman in the military."

"As a woman in the military, recruiters hesitate putting us on the frontline.  It was banned until 2013 because men cant stay on task if we get injured. Instinct is to save women and that may steer off from the task. You need to be in another trade to be a woman in the military."

"As a woman in the military, you dont get the issued necessities. Men get issued underwear while woman have to bring their own. Dont even get me started about bras. You need to spend more money than a man to be a woman in the military."

"As a woman in the military, you have to strive for the same level of fitness as men. The test is built for men that can lift heavy, Affecting womens ability to score as high as a man. You need to be as fit as a man to be a woman in the military."

"As a woman in the military, you share accommodations with males on your course. With 2 minutes to change, the males can change by their lockers, But women have to run to the bathroom so they are not stared at. You need to wear an under layer to be a woman in the military."

"As a woman in the military, you need to know that tradition is important. If I try to change something in my own department,  People think I am disrupting what "our veterans have fought for." You need to follow tradition to be a woman in the military."

"As a woman in the military, I deserve the respect that comes with my rank. If I am walking down the street with a male subordinate officer,  People assume he is a higher rank than me. You need to show your rank to be a woman in the military."

"As a woman in the military, subordinate male officers will question my orders. If they dont like what I am saying, they will find a man that will side with them. They will undermine you in front of others.  You need to know your facts to be a woman in the military."

"As a woman in the military, I have to go through development to take command. Have been a Captain for 6 years; have more experience than others, But they will give the position to a man with no experience. You need to be okay with a man taking over to be a woman in the military."

"As a woman in the military, I am allowed to be the Deputy Commanding Officer, But I cant be the Commanding Officer. My chain of command says I am unapproachable because I say whats on my mind. You need to be approachable to be a woman in the military."

"As a woman in the military, I am finding myself having to change who I am. If I express my opinion, I am aggressive and bossy, If I am too quiet, I am not vocal enough to be taken seriously. You need to show less emotion to be a woman in the military."
